title: The Bay Before 1769
text: Tidal marsh rings the bay and oaks stand over grassland. About a hundred villages of Ohlone, Miwok, Pomo, Wappo and Patwin people line the creeks and shores.
note: [Region] Terrain c.1800 cover (SFEI baylands / historical ecology, decision 12); 105 contact-era villages: data/manual/ohlone/villages.csv (75), data/tables/early_sf.csv yel_* (5), early_region.csv (25).

title: Chutchui, a Yelamu Village
text: The Yelamu, 160 to 300 people, live at the tip of the peninsula and move with the seasons between tule-house villages such as Chutchui, on Mission Creek.
note: [SF] early_sf.csv yel_chutchui (1700-1784.4; position approximate, houses drawn at 2x); population.csv 1769 san_francisco (Milliken: 160-300).

title: Portolá Sights the Bay
text: 4 November 1769: Gaspar de Portolá's overland expedition views the bay from Sweeney Ridge. Sgt. José Ortega's scouts had first seen it three days earlier.
note: [Peninsula] events.csv 1769-11-04 Portolá Sights the Bay (lat/lon of the event); places.csv Sweeney Ridge label from 1769.

title: Through the Golden Gate
text: 5 August 1775: Juan Manuel de Ayala's San Carlos sails in past the white cliff, the first European ship known to enter the bay.
note: [SF] events.csv 1775-08-05 Through the Golden Gate; landmarks.csv punta_del_cantil_blanco (the white cliff at the strait, 1700-1853). No ship is drawn.

title: The Presidio of San Francisco
text: 17 September 1776: Spain founds its northernmost outpost. Its 193 soldiers and settlers build a wooden chapel, a storehouse and thatched quarters.
note: [SF] events.csv 1776-09-17 Presidio Founded; landmarks.csv el_presidio_1776 (palisade presidio 1776-1781); population.csv 1776 presidio = 193.

title: Mission Dolores
text: Founded on 9 October 1776, the mission finishes its adobe church in 1791; it still stands. Adobe rows rise beside it for the neophytes, some 1,100 at the peak.
note: [SF] events.csv 1776-10-09 Mission Dolores; landmarks.csv mission_dolores (model built 1782.5-1791.5), mission_dolores_quadrangle_* (1794-95), mission_dolores_rancheria_1..4 (1793-1798; rows 5-8 to 1806 follow after the stop); population.csv 1815 mission_dolores = 1,100 (1810-1820 peak).

title: Mission Santa Clara and San José
text: Flooded out in 1779, Mission Santa Clara now stands on its third site. The Pueblo de San José, founded nearby in 1777, has 171 people in 1800.
note: [South Bay] early_region.csv scl_m1_* (first site 1777.03-1779.86, flooded 23 Jan 1779), scl_m3_* (third site: church 1781.88-, ranges, rancheria rows 1793-1806), sj_pv_houses_1777 (pueblo 1777.91); population_places.csv San Jose 1800 = 171. The pueblo itself (4.5 km SE) is not in this view.

title: Fort Ross
text: 1812: Ivan Kuskov of the Russian-American Company lands 25 Russians and 80 Alaskans at Metini, in Kashaya Pomo country, and builds a redwood stockade.
note: [North Bay] landmarks_northbay.csv fort_ross_stockade_1812 (model built 1812.2-1812.7), fort_ross_russian_buildings (1812.2-1814.0); villages.csv kas_metini (Metini, to 1870). The chapel (c.1825) comes after this stop.

title: Rancho San Antonio
text: Luis María Peralta's Rancho San Antonio, granted in 1820, runs from San Leandro Creek to today's Berkeley. His son Antonio builds this adobe in 1821.
note: [East Bay] early_region.csv ala_peralta_shelter_1820 (1820.6-1822.0), ala_peralta_adobe_1821 (1821.8-1897.5; note: Rancho San Antonio granted to Luis Maria Peralta 1820); the other Peralta adobes of the rancho (San Leandro Creek, Temescal, Codornices Creek in Berkeley) are in the same table. Open grassland before 1850: decision 13b.

title: Yerba Buena
text: June 1835: William Richardson pitches a tent above the cove. Yerba Buena has some 200 people when the U.S. flag goes up in 1846; from January 1847 it is San Francisco.
note: [SF] early_sf.csv yb_* (Richardson tent 1835.45, Leese 1836, Casa Grande 1837.5, Custom House 1845.7 ...); events.csv 1835, 1846-07-09, 1847-01-30; places.csv sf_yerba_buena (1835-1847) -> sf_san_francisco_1847 (label changes during the stop); population.csv 1846 = 200.

title: Sonoma and the Bear Flag
text: The last mission, founded in 1823, and Mariano Vallejo's barracks face Sonoma's plaza. On 14 June 1846 the Bear Flag party makes the barracks its headquarters.
note: [North Bay] landmarks_northbay.csv mission_san_francisco_solano_convento (1832-), mission_san_francisco_solano_chapel (1841-), sonoma_barracks (1841-; notes: Bear Flag Party headquarters 14 June 1846).

title: Gold Rush: the Cove Fills In
text: Gold is found in January 1848; the town of 800 holds 25,000 by December 1849. Fill moves the shore from Montgomery Street out to Battery Street by 1853.
note: [SF] fill_zones.csv sf_ybc_1_montgomery_sansome (1849-1851.7), sf_ybc_2_sansome_battery (1850-1853); events.csv 1848-01-24 Gold!; population.csv 1848 = 812, 1849.92 = 25,000; buildings: OHM gold-rush outlines + sf_extent_1849/1852 fabric. Ships are not drawn.

title: Fire and Brick
text: The fire of 4 May 1851 burns the heart of the wooden city, which rebuilds in brick. The four-storey Montgomery Block of 1853 is the tallest building in the West.
note: [SF] OHM gold-rush buildings end 1851.34 on the Burnt District map of the 4 May 1851 fire (decision 39; 75 outlines); landmarks.csv montgomery_block (1853-1959) / notable_pre1906.csv montgomery_block_1853; sf_extent 1852/1856 brick massing.

title: Benicia, State Capital
text: From 3 February 1853 to 24 February 1854 the Legislature meets in Benicia's brick city hall, California's third capitol, before moving to Sacramento.
note: [Solano-Delta] landmarks_northbay.csv benicia_capitol (1852-).

title: Mare Island Navy Yard
text: 1854: the Navy starts a shipyard on Mare Island, across the strait from Vallejo. Its first shops go up in 1854–58; the yard works until 1996.
note: [Solano-Delta] industrial_sites/sites.geojson mare_island (1854-; shops of 1854-58, label over its years); known_dates_industrial.csv footprints; closure 1996: CLAUDE.md decision 42.

title: Fort Point
text: The Army has cut down the white cliff of the Spanish castillo and builds a masonry fort at the water's edge, finished in 1861.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv punta_del_cantil_blanco and castillo_de_san_joaquin (end 1853), fort_point (model built 1853.5-1861.0: frame during the stop).

title: The Delta Is Diked
text: April 1869: a levee closes round Sherman Island, the first peat island of the Delta leveed completely. Twitchell, Brannan and Jersey islands follow by 1873.
note: [Solano-Delta] fill_zones.csv dl_sherman_island (1868-1869), dl_twitchell_island (1869), dl_brannan_andrus (1871-72), dl_jersey_island (1872-73), dl_bradford_island (1871); data/manual/delta/ (Thompson 1957). Terrain cover only at this zoom.

title: The Railroad Reaches Oakland
text: 8 November 1869: the transcontinental railroad ends on Oakland's Long Wharf, where ferries meet the trains. Oakland has 34,555 people by 1880.
note: [East Bay] routes.csv rr_cp_long_wharf (1869-1919; terminus from 1869-11-08), fy_oakland_pier (1869-1958), rr_sp_oakland_mole (1882); fill_zones.csv al_oakland_long_wharf_mole_* (1868-1882); population_places.csv Oakland 1870, 1880; West Oakland footprints (622 before 1880, 2,813 before 1890).

title: Golden Gate Park
text: 4 April 1870: Golden Gate Park is established on 1,017 acres, three-quarters of them bare dunes. Planting advances from the east toward the ocean.
note: [SF] events.csv 1870-04-04 Golden Gate Park; landmarks.csv golden_gate_park (1870-), conservatory_of_flowers (1879); data/research/parks_dates.md (1,017 acres, three-quarters dunes); woods dated east to west (decision 9); dunes.geojson.

title: The First Cable Car
text: 2 August 1873: Andrew Hallidie's Clay Street Hill Railroad makes its first run, up Clay Street from Kearny to Jones.
note: [SF] events.csv 1873-08-02 First Cable Car; routes.csv cc_clay_hill (Clay St, Kearny - Leavenworth, 1873-1942; the route row is dated 1873.0, so the line is already drawn at the start of the year).

title: The Palace Hotel
text: 2 October 1875: William Ralston's Palace Hotel opens on Market Street, seven storeys and 755 rooms, the largest hotel in the American West.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv palace_hotel_1875 (1875-1906) / notable_pre1906.csv palace_hotel_1875.

title: Nob Hill
text: Railroad and silver fortunes crown the hill: the Stanford, Crocker and Hopkins mansions go up in 1876–78. Only James Flood's, of 1886, will outlast 1906.
note: [SF] notable_pre1906.csv stanford_mansion_1876, crocker_mansion_1877, hopkins_mansion_1878, huntington_colton_mansion_1872 (all end 1906), flood_mansion_1886 (survives; appears after this stop); routes.csv cc_california (1878-).

title: The Valley of Orchards
text: From the 1870s orchards replace wheat on the floor of the Santa Clara Valley, spreading out from San José, a town of 12,567 in 1880.
note: [South Bay] data/manual/landscape/agriculture.geojson + README: scv_san_jose orchards 1872->1890, scv_campbell_los_gatos 1878->95, grain eras 1852-62 before; population_places.csv San Jose 1880. Terrain cover (orchard pattern, decision 31) at this zoom; buildings load only from zoom 12.5.

title: Stanford University
text: The cornerstone is laid on 14 May 1887. Twelve one-storey sandstone buildings round the Inner Quad are ready when the university opens on 1 October 1891.
note: [Peninsula] landmarks_southbay.csv stanford_inner_quad (construction 1887.37-1891.75).

title: Napa Valley Wine
text: Vineyards have spread up the Napa Valley since the late 1860s. Greystone Cellars, built at St. Helena in 1888–89 of local tufa, is 400 feet long.
note: [North Bay] landmarks_northbay.csv greystone_cellars (1889-), beringer_rhine_house (1884) 600 m south; agriculture.geojson napa_valley_mid vineyard era 1868->1885.

title: Victorians of the Western Addition
text: Wooden row houses fill the blocks west of Van Ness Avenue, drawn here from the 1899 Sanborn maps; the seven Painted Ladies go up in 1892–96.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv painted_ladies (1894-), alamo_square (1857-); Sanborn tracing of the Western Addition 1899 + 1913 (decision 27; 6,057 traced footprints, source sanborn_western_addition).

title: The Cliff House and Sutro Baths
text: The first Cliff House burns on Christmas Day 1894. A seven-storey chateau replaces it in 1896, the year the Sutro Baths open just to the north.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv cliff_house_1863 (model end 1894.98, Christmas 1894), cliff_house_1896 (built 1895.6-1896.2, to 1907), sutro_baths (built 1894.3-1896.2, opened 1896-03-14), sutro_heights_mansion (1885-1939).

title: The Ferry Building
text: 13 July 1898: A. Page Brown's Ferry Building opens at the foot of Market Street under a 245-foot clock tower. Ferries from Oakland, Alameda and Sausalito land here.
note: [SF] events.csv 1898-07-13 Ferry Building Opens; landmarks.csv ferry_building (model built 1896.0-1898.53); routes.csv fy_oakland_pier, fy_alameda_pier, fy_sausalito, fy_creek_route. Camera point is 100 m inland of the building: the terrain land-year grid dates the ground under the building itself to c.1923.

title: The City in 1905
text: San Francisco counts 342,782 people in 1900. The 315-foot Call Building on Market Street is the tallest west of Chicago; City Hall's dome dates from 1899.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv call_building_1898, city_hall_1899 (position approximate, LOW CONFIDENCE model), palace_hotel_1875, old_mint; sf_extent_1905 fabric; population.csv 1900.

title: 18 April 1906
text: At 5:12 a.m. a magnitude 7.9 earthquake strikes. Fire burns until 21 April and destroys about 28,000 buildings, from the waterfront to Van Ness Avenue.
note: [SF] events.csv 1906-04-18 The Great Earthquake; data/manual/fire_1906_boundary.csv (ring = 2,569 acres); ~15,700 predecessor buildings end at 1906.29 (sf_predecessors); terrain burn cover is instant. 28,000 buildings: CLAUDE.md pitfall 1. events.csv says "four days" (18-21 April).

title: Where the Fire Stopped
text: The fire is held at Van Ness Avenue, Dolores Street and 20th Street. West of Dolores the mission's adobe church of 1791 survives, with the houses around it.
note: [SF] data/manual/fire_1906_README.md (lines held at Van Ness, Dolores, 20th St); landmarks.csv mission_dolores (1791-9999).

title: Santa Rosa, 1906
text: The same earthquake wrecks Santa Rosa, a town of 6,673: its business district falls or burns and about a hundred people die. A new courthouse stands by 1909.
note: [North Bay] data/manual/fires/quake_1906_santa_rosa.geojson (outline ESTIMATED, year 1906.29); Sanborn tracings of downtown Santa Rosa 1904 / 1908; notable_demolished_region.csv sr_sonoma_county_courthouse_1884 (-1906), sr_sonoma_county_courthouse_1909; population_places.csv Santa Rosa 1900. The map shows the aftermath (buildings end at 1906.29, before this stop begins).

title: The City Rebuilds
text: The ruins are cleared and the burned district fills again within a few years. The Palace Hotel reopens in 1909; the city counts 416,912 people in 1910.
note: [SF] sf_buildings (burned core: 136 of today's buildings by 1907, 798 by 1910, 997 by 1912) + sf_rebuild_procedural predecessors; landmarks.csv palace_hotel_1909, fairmont_hotel (1907); population.csv 1910.

title: Berkeley's Campus
text: The University of California builds its core: Sather Gate in 1910, Doe Library in 1911 and in 1915 Sather Tower, a 307-foot campanile.
note: [East Bay] landmarks_eastbay.csv sather_gate (1910), doe_library_1911, doe_library_1917, sather_tower (1915), hearst_greek_theatre (1903).

title: Oakland Grows Up
text: Since 1903 Key System trains have run to a ferry pier three miles out in the bay. Oakland, 150,174 people in 1910, builds a 320-foot City Hall in 1910–14.
note: [East Bay] landmarks_eastbay.csv oakland_city_hall (1910-14), cathedral_building_oakland (1914), tribune_building_1906; routes.csv ks_mole (1903-1939, ~16,000 ft), ks_* lines; Sanborn tracing of downtown Oakland 1912; population_places.csv Oakland 1910.

title: The Panama-Pacific Exposition
text: From April 1912 dredges pump sand into the cove at Harbor View. On 20 February 1915 a world's fair opens on the new ground, round the 435-foot Tower of Jewels.
note: [SF] fill_zones.csv sf_marina_cove_1912 (1912.28-1912.7), sf_marina_west_ppie; events.csv 1915-02-20 (636-acre site); landmarks.csv ppie_* (30 models traced from the 1914 Sanborn; Tower of Jewels built 1914.0-1915.13), palace_of_fine_arts_1915; places.csv Harbor View (1864-1912). Camera point on the pre-1912 shore, the fill lies north of it.

title: A New City Hall
text: Construction starts on 5 April 1913, west of the site of the ruined old hall. The new City Hall opens in December 1915 under a dome 307 feet high.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv city_hall_1915 (construction from 1913-04-05, opened Dec 1915), civic_auditorium (1915); city_hall_1899 (-1906, position approximate).

title: The Twin Peaks Tunnel
text: 3 February 1918: streetcars start running through a 3.56-kilometre tunnel under Twin Peaks. West Portal and St. Francis Wood grow up at its western mouth.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv twin_peaks_tunnel (west portal, opened 1918-02-03, 3.56 km); places.csv West Portal (1918-), Forest Hill (1912-), St. Francis Wood (1912-); DataSF footprints with assessor years.

title: From Fairground to the Marina
text: The fair closed on 4 December 1915 and its palaces came down in 1916. Only the Palace of Fine Arts stays; houses cover the filled cove in the 1920s.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv ppie_* end 1916, palace_of_fine_arts_1915 (-1964); sf_buildings in the Marina: 689 before 1920, 1,137 before 1925, 2,303 before 1930; places.csv Marina District (1916-).

title: The Santa Cruz Boardwalk
text: Beside the Casino of 1907, the Giant Dipper opens on 17 May 1924: a wooden roller coaster with 2,640 feet of track and a 70-foot lift hill.
note: [Santa Cruz] landmarks_coastsouth.csv giant_dipper_santa_cruz (construction 1924.25-1924.38, on its track), boardwalk_casino (1907), boardwalk_plunge (1907), looff_carousel_santa_cruz (1911), santa_cruz_wharf (1914).

title: The Skyline of the Twenties
text: The Pacific Telephone Building opens on 30 May 1925; the Russ Building follows in 1927. Both reach 435 feet, the city's tallest until 1964.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv new_montgomery_140 (1925), russ_building (1927; city's tallest 1927-1964 with the 435 ft Pacific Telephone Building), mark_hopkins (1926).

title: The Carquinez Bridge
text: 21 May 1927: the Carquinez Bridge is dedicated, a steel cantilever with two 1,100-foot main spans on the direct road from the bay cities to Sacramento.
note: [Solano-Delta] landmarks_northbay.csv carquinez_bridge_1927 (1927-2007; built 1923-27); routes.csv br_carquinez_1927; industrial site ch_crockett (C&H sugar refinery, 1906-) at the south end. Camera point is over the strait (bridge).

title: Mills Field
text: 7 May 1927: San Francisco dedicates an airport on 150 acres of leased cow pasture, once tidal marsh. In the 1930s fill carries it out over the tidelands.
note: [Peninsula] airports.csv San Francisco International Airport (opened 1927, dedicated 7 May 1927); fill_zones.csv sm_sfo_mills_pasture_field (the 150-acre lease), sm_sfo_tidelands_1930s (1930.5-1935); decision 30 (dirt Runway B 1927, Runway C 1928 / 1935).

title: Seals Stadium
text: 7 April 1931: the Seals open a roofless concrete ballpark at 16th and Bryant. The Giants play here in 1958 and 1959, and then it is torn down.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv seals_stadium (1931-1959; opened 1931-04-07, demolished Nov 1959). Giants 1958-59 and "Bryant & 16th", "no roof": checked on the cited Wikipedia page (2026-11), not in the repo tables.

title: Hangar One
text: At the Navy's new air station at Sunnyvale, a hangar 1,133 feet long and 198 feet high is built in 1931–33 for the airship USS Macon.
note: [South Bay] landmarks_southbay.csv hangar_one_1933 (construction 1931.8-1933.6); airports.csv Moffett Federal Airfield (1933).

title: Coit Tower
text: 8 October 1933: a 210-foot tower designed by Arthur Brown Jr. and paid for by Lillie Hitchcock Coit's bequest is dedicated on the summit of Telegraph Hill.
note: [SF] events.csv 1933-10-08 Coit Tower; landmarks.csv coit_tower (built 1932-33).

title: The Bay Bridge
text: Work begins on 9 July 1933. On 12 November 1936 the bridge opens: two suspension spans to Yerba Buena Island, then a cantilever and trusses on to Oakland.
note: [SF] events.csv 1936-11-12 Bay Bridge Opens; landmarks.csv bay_bridge_west_span (1936-), bay_bridge_east_span_1936 (1936-2017; 1936 east-span alignment LOW CONFIDENCE); routes.csv fwy_i80_bay_bridge. Camera point = centre anchorage, over water (bridge).

title: Alcatraz
text: 11 August 1934: the Army cellhouse of 1912 reopens as a federal penitentiary. The island, lit by a lighthouse since 1854, holds prisoners until 1963.
note: [SF] events.csv 1934-08-11 Alcatraz Penitentiary; landmarks.csv alcatraz_cellhouse (1912-), alcatraz_lighthouse_1909, alcatraz_lighthouse_1854 (1854-1909). Camera point 100 m NE of the cellhouse anchor: the 30 m terrain grid has the island there.

title: The Golden Gate Bridge
text: Begun on 5 January 1933, the bridge opens to walkers on 27 May 1937 and to cars the next day. Its towers stand 746 feet above the strait.
note: [SF] events.csv 1937-05-27 Golden Gate Bridge Opens; landmarks.csv golden_gate_bridge (construction from 1933-01-05; stands in unpainted steel while being built, decision 25). Camera point = mid-span, over water (bridge).

title: Treasure Island
text: From February 1936 Army engineers raise 400 acres of sand on the shoals off Yerba Buena Island. A world's fair opens there on 18 February 1939.
note: [SF] fill_zones.csv sf_treasure_island (1936.1-1937.65, begun 11 Feb 1936, ~400 acres); events.csv 1939-02-18 Treasure Island Fair; landmarks.csv ggie_* (10 models; Tower of the Sun 400 ft, not named in the caption), treasure_island_building_1 (1938). Camera point on the north shore of Yerba Buena Island (natural land); the fill lies north of it, toward the camera.

title: Richmond's Shipyards
text: From December 1940 Kaiser builds four shipyards on filled tideland at Richmond; they launch 747 ships. The city of 23,642 has 99,545 people by 1950.
note: [East Bay] industrial_sites kaiser_yards_1_2 (1941-1946), kaiser_yard3 (1942-); fill_zones.csv cc_richmond_shipyards (1940.9-1942; Yard 1 begun Dec 1940), cc_richmond_shipyard3; landmarks_ports.csv kaiser_yard3_whirley_cranes (1942.1-1946; 747 ships, NPS); landmarks_eastbay.csv ford_richmond_assembly_plant (1931); population_places.csv Richmond 1940, 1950. Camera point on 1920 harbour fill between the yards.

title: Hunters Point
text: The Navy levels a 170-foot hill at Hunters Point and moves 5 million cubic yards of it into the bay. A 1,092-foot dry dock is dug in 1942–43.
note: [SF] fill_zones.csv sf_hunters_point_navy_wwii (1942-1945; Dow pp.139-145: 170-ft hill, 5 million yd3, 1,092-ft dry dock 1942-43); landmarks_ports.csv hunters_point_drydock_4 (1943), drydocks 2 and 3; the gantry crane (1947) comes after the stop.

title: The Sunset Fills In
text: Rows of houses have crossed the dunes south of Golden Gate Park since the 1920s. After the war the last sand lots fill in; the city has 775,357 people in 1950.
note: [SF] sf_buildings (assessor years) in the Sunset: 4,304 footprints before 1925, 14,756 before 1940, 25,910 before 1950 of 30,602; dunes.geojson; population.csv 1950.

title: Orchards to Suburbs
text: Tracts replace the orchards that covered some 100,000 acres of the Santa Clara Valley. San José grows from 95,280 people in 1950 to 459,913 in 1970.
note: [South Bay] agriculture.geojson topo_1940s orchards (real, USGS 1939-56) ending as cells become city; region footprints Sunnyvale - Santa Clara - Cupertino: 12,983 before 1950, 42,612 before 1960, 60,320 before 1970; population_places.csv San Jose 1950, 1970. 100,000 acres: CLAUDE.md pitfall 6 (not in a data table). Buildings load only from zoom 12.5: terrain cover (orchard -> suburban ground) at this zoom.

title: Redevelopment in the Fillmore
text: On 28 May 1956 the city makes 27 blocks of the Western Addition a redevelopment area. Victorian rows come down and about 8,000 residents are evicted.
note: [SF] redevelopment_areas.csv wa_a1 (clear 1956-1963 ESTIMATED; ~8,000 evicted; Geary Expressway demolition 1960), wa_a2 (1966-1973); Sanborn-traced fabric ends at the clearance (decision 19/27).

title: The Embarcadero Freeway
text: 5 February 1959: a double-deck freeway opens across the front of the Ferry Building. That January the supervisors' freeway revolt had blocked further routes.
note: [SF] events.csv 1959-02-05 Embarcadero Freeway; landmarks.csv embarcadero_freeway (1959-1991; route LOW CONFIDENCE) / routes.csv fwy_embarcadero.

title: Candlestick Park
text: Ground is broken on 12 August 1958 on tideland filled with rock from Bay View Hill. The stadium, all of reinforced concrete, opens on 12 April 1960.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv candlestick_park_1960 (1960-1971); fill_zones.csv sf_candlestick_park (1956-1960.3; Dow pp.155-156); data/research/landmarks.md (first all-reinforced-concrete MLB stadium). Part of the site is still bay at the start of the stop (the fill is under way).

title: Marin County Civic Center
text: 15 February 1960: ground is broken for Frank Lloyd Wright's last major commission, a 580-foot building bridging between hills. It is dedicated on 13 October 1962.
note: [Marin] landmarks_southbay.csv marin_civic_center_admin (construction 1960.12-1962.78); Hall of Justice 1969 follows.

title: Foster City
text: Brewer Island, diked for pasture about 1900, is raised with 18 million cubic yards of dredged sand. The first residents of Foster City arrive on 7 March 1964.
note: [Peninsula] fill_zones.csv sm_foster_city_diked (1897-1901), sm_foster_city_fill (1961-1971; 18 million yd3, first residents 7 Mar 1964); water_history.csv Foster City Lagoon (1963); region footprints: 1,896 before 1965, 4,130 before 1970; places.csv smc_foster_city (1964-); routes.csv br_san_mateo_1967.

title: Containers at Oakland
text: Sea-Land has run container ships from Oakland's Outer Harbor since September 1962. The port's first two container cranes go up in 1966.
note: [East Bay] industrial_sites oakland_port_terminals (1962.7-; Sea-Land service from 5 Sep 1962); landmarks_ports.csv oak_yard_sealand (1962), oak_sealand_cranes_1966 (built 1965.8-1966.4) / _1968, oak_7th_street_cranes_1968 (1969) / _1972, oak_crane_x421 (1968); fill_zones.csv tp_oakland_7th_street_1958_1968, _1968_1973.

title: The Transamerica Pyramid
text: On the site of the Montgomery Block an 853-foot pyramid is built from December 1969 to 1972. It passes the 779-foot Bank of America tower as the city's tallest.
note: [SF] events.csv 1972 Transamerica Pyramid (853 ft); landmarks.csv transamerica_pyramid (construction from Dec 1969), california_555 (1969, 779 ft, tallest until 1972), montgomery_block (-1959).

title: BART
text: 11 September 1972: the first BART trains run between Fremont and Oakland's MacArthur station. The tube under the bay opens on 16 September 1974.
note: [East Bay] transit_openings.csv bart_fremont_macarthur (1972-09-11), bart_transbay (1974-09-16); bart_macarthur_richmond, bart_macarthur_concord, bart_montgomery_daly_city (1973) open during the stop; events.csv 1974-09-16 BART Under the Bay; trains and stations per decision 24.

title: Embarcadero Center
text: On the cleared produce market, the four towers of Embarcadero Center go up between 1971 and 1982, with the Hyatt Regency of 1973 at the waterfront end.
note: [SF] landmarks.csv embarcadero_center_1 (1971), _2 (1974), _3 (1977), _4 (1982), hyatt_regency (1973), california_101 (1982); redevelopment_areas.csv golden_gateway (produce market cleared from c.1960).

title: Loma Prieta: the Cypress Viaduct
text: 17 October 1989, 5:04 p.m.: a magnitude 6.9 earthquake. In West Oakland the upper deck of the double-deck Cypress Street Viaduct falls on the lower; 42 people die.
note: [East Bay] routes.csv fwy_cypress (1957.44-1989.79; note: collapsed 1989-10-17, 42 deaths): the viaduct leaves the map on the day of the earthquake, about half way through the stop. events.csv 1989-10-17.

title: Loma Prieta: Santa Cruz
text: The earthquake is centred ten miles away in the mountains. Pacific Avenue loses the Cooper House of 1895, the Hotel Metropole and the St. George Hotel.
note: [Santa Cruz] notable_demolished_region.csv scz_cooper_house_1895 (-1989.82, demolition began c. 26 Oct 1989), scz_hotel_metropole_1908 (-1989.88, estimate), scz_st_george_hotel_1895 (-1990): all three leave the map during the stop. Epicentre ~10 miles NE of Santa Cruz: checked on the cited Wikipedia page (2026-11), not in the repo.

title: Loma Prieta: the Marina
text: In San Francisco the damage is worst in the Marina, on the sand pumped into the cove in 1912: the fill liquefies, seven buildings collapse and four burn.
note: [SF] events.csv 1989-10-17 Loma Prieta Earthquake (Marina, Bay Bridge deck section); fill_zones.csv sf_marina_cove_1912 (note: liquefied in 1989). The map shows the district on its fill but no damage. "Seven buildings collapsed, four destroyed by fire": checked on the cited Wikipedia page (2026-11), not in the repo.

title: The Freeway Comes Down
text: The Embarcadero Freeway, closed since the earthquake, never reopens. Demolition starts on 27 February 1991, and the Ferry Building faces Market Street again.
note: [SF] events.csv 1991-02-27 The Freeway Comes Down; landmarks model embarcadero_freeway ends 1991.3 (leaves the map during the stop) / routes.csv fwy_embarcadero (1959-1991).

title: The Oakland Hills Firestorm
text: 20 October 1991: a wind-driven fire above the Caldecott Tunnel burns 1,520 acres of the Oakland and Berkeley hills, kills 25 people and destroys 2,843 houses.
note: [East Bay] events.csv 1991-10-20 Oakland Hills Firestorm; redevelopment_areas.csv fire_tunnel_1991 (dated clearance 1991.8, FRAP perimeter); region footprints in the area: ~340 new by 1994, ~1,130 by 1996, ~1,470 by 2000.

title: A Ballpark at China Basin
text: 31 March 2000: the Giants open Pacific Bell Park, now Oracle Park, at China Basin. It is the first major-league ballpark built without public funds since 1962.
note: [SF] events.csv 2000-03-31 Pac Bell Park Opens; landmarks.csv oracle_park (groundbreaking 1997-12-11, opened 2000-03-31); transit_openings.csv muni_metro_extension (1998).

title: A New East Span
text: 2 September 2013: a new eastern span of the Bay Bridge opens, a single-tower suspension bridge and a skyway. The 1936 cantilever is dismantled by 2017.
note: [East Bay] events.csv 2013-09-02 New Bay Bridge Span; landmark models bay_bridge_east_2013_sas (built 2009.0-2013.67), _skyway (2002.08-2007.5), bay_bridge_east_1936_cantilever (end 2015.45), _trusses (2016.6), _causeway (2017.2); landmarks.csv bay_bridge_east_span_2013, bay_bridge_east_span_1936. Camera point = SAS tower, over water (bridge).

title: Apple Park
text: Hewlett-Packard's Cupertino campus stood here from 1969, on former orchard land. Apple replaces it with a ring 1,512 feet across, occupied from April 2017.
note: [South Bay] landmarks_southbay.csv apple_park_ring (construction 2013.9-2017.3), steve_jobs_theater, apple_park_visitor_center; vanished_sites hp_cupertino (1969-2014), apple_park grounds (2017.3-); agriculture.geojson topo_1940s orchard at the site.

title: Salesforce Tower
text: Salesforce Tower, 61 floors and 1,070 feet, opens on 8 January 2018 as the city's tallest building. The transit center beside it follows on 12 August.
note: [SF] events.csv 2018-08-12 Salesforce Transit Center; landmarks.csv salesforce_tower (groundbreaking 2013-03-27, opened 2018-01-08; height_m 326.1), salesforce_transit_center (2018), fremont_181 (2018), millennium_tower (2009), transbay_terminal_1939 (-2011).

title: Mission Bay and Chase Center
text: Since 1998 the rail yards of Mission Bay have become a district of laboratories, housing and a UCSF campus. Chase Center opens there on 6 September 2019.
note: [SF] redevelopment_areas.csv mission_bay (cleared 1998-2008; UCSF groundbreaking 1999); landmarks model chase_center built 2017.05-2019.68 (opened 2019-09-06); sf_buildings in Mission Bay: 168 before 2000, 421 before 2010, 584 before 2020; fill_zones.csv sf_mission_bay_* (1869-1912).

title: The Tubbs Fire
text: 9 October 2017: the Tubbs Fire runs from Calistoga into Santa Rosa overnight. More than 1,300 homes burn in Coffey Park; most are rebuilt by 2021.
note: [North Bay] events.csv 2017-10-09 North Bay Firestorm; data/manual/fires/destroyed_structures.csv tubbs_2017 = 5,656 (Coffey Park: 1,432 structures, 1,355 of them dwellings); fire_dates.csv tubbs_2017 (started near Tubbs Lane, Calistoga, 8 Oct); region footprints in Coffey Park: 3,363 before 2018, 3,750 before 2019, 4,396 before 2020, 4,644 before 2021 (rebuild classes per decision 42).

title: The CZU Lightning Complex
text: Lightning on 16 August 2020 starts fires in the Santa Cruz Mountains that merge two days later and destroy 1,490 buildings around Boulder Creek and Bonny Doon.
note: [Santa Cruz] events.csv 2020-08-18 CZU Lightning Complex; destroyed_structures.csv czu_2020 = 1,490 (camera on the densest cluster, Bonny Doon / Empire Grade, 7 km from the event point; structures dated 2020-08-19 in fire_dates.csv); open country is not drawn burned (decision 42).

title: The Bay Area Today
text: Two and a half centuries after Portolá's scouts saw the bay, 7,765,640 people (2020) live in the nine counties around it, on shores reshaped by fill and dikes.
note: [Region] population.csv bay_area_9county 2020 = 7,765,640; fill_zones.csv (303 dated zones incl. restored: sm_bair_island_restored, nb_napa_ponds_restored, sb_island_ponds_restored); map extent = ten counties (decision 32).
